title: A method, device, equipment and storage medium for hierarchical federated learning of electricity consumption data

pse.problem: Limited enthusiasm of participants due to existing federal learning framework deficiencies: high time consumption in synchronous aggregation, non-comprehensive reward mechanism, lack of consideration for task publishers rewards and benefits, unsuitable rewarding form.
pse.solution_function: A hierarchical federal learning method facilitates privacy protection and data island resolution by enabling model training on local equipment without exposing user data. The system coordinates between participants (home energy management systems and load integrators) for real-time electricity data collection, local training, parameter updates, asynchronous local aggregation, and issuance of local aggregation parameters.
pse.solution_structure: The system consists of participating units (home energy management systems and load integrators), each home energy management system collects real-time electricity data and performs local training based on it to update local model parameters, which are then submitted to the corresponding load integrator.
pse.solution_implementation: In this method, a participant obtains initial model parameters and begins training based on these parameters. The household energy management system collects real-time electricity data and conducts local training using it to update the local model parameters. These updated local model parameters are submitted to the load integrator in the corresponding area. The load integrator performs asynchronous local aggregation based on the local model parameters and the current global model parameters to obtain local aggregation parameters.
pse.effect: By addressing the deficiencies of existing federal learning frameworks, this solution promotes increased participation enthusiasm due to reduced time consumption, a more comprehensive reward mechanism, consideration for task publishers rewards and benefits, and a suitable rewarding form.
